notes.meaning: Jesus walks out of the temple for the last time. His public teaching there is over. His disciples, amazed by the huge, beautiful stones and buildings, want Him to admire them too. Herod had spent great sums on this temple, and it was one of the wonders of the world.

Jesus does not share their wonder. He tells them plainly that the whole temple will be torn down, stone by stone. When it was said, this seemed impossible. About forty years later, in AD 70, the Roman army under Titus burned it and dug up its foundations. Even the finest things of this world will not last, so we should not set our hearts on them.

From the Mount of Olives they could look across at the temple. A few disciples ask Jesus privately when this will happen. They also ask what sign will show His coming and the end of the age. They seem to think the temple's fall and the end of the world are the same event. In His answer, Jesus speaks of both: the coming fall of Jerusalem, and His return at the end of time.

Jesus does not give them a date. Instead, He starts with a warning: don't let anyone trick you. He cares more about keeping them safe and faithful than about satisfying their curiosity. This warning runs through the whole talk.

Many people will come claiming to be the Christ, God's promised King, and many will believe them. Before Jerusalem fell, several such fakes did appear, and people followed them. Others have made the same claim in later times.

There will be wars near and far, and news of wars. But Jesus tells His followers not to panic. These things are part of God's plan, and they do not mean the end has come yet. A heart that trusts God can stay at peace even in troubled times.

Nations and kingdoms will fight one another. There will be famines and earthquakes in many places. Commentators point to fighting between Jews and their neighbors, a famine in the days of Claudius (Acts 11:28), and several earthquakes in the years before AD 70.

These troubles are only the first pains, like a woman's first labor pains before a baby is born. Harder times are still ahead. They are not a sign that the end has arrived, only that things have begun.

Jesus warns His followers that they will be handed over, hurt, and some even killed. People everywhere will hate them simply because they belong to Jesus. The book of Acts shows this coming true with Stephen, James, Peter, Paul and others.
When following Jesus becomes costly, many will give up their faith. Some who turn away will even betray and hate those who stay faithful. Hard times show who really belongs to Christ.
Many false prophets will rise up and lead people astray. These are teachers who claim to speak for God but do not. Jesus warns that such teachers will trouble the church in every age.
As wickedness spreads, many people's love will grow cold. This means their love for God and for one another fades. Yet it is "many," not all. God always keeps some who stay warm and faithful.

Here is comfort in the middle of the warnings. Whoever keeps trusting Jesus to the end will be saved. Most commentators take this to mean final salvation in heaven for those who stay faithful until the end of their lives.

Even with all this trouble, the good news of God's kingdom will be preached to all nations. Some commentators say this happened in a broad way before AD 70, and then "the end" of the old temple system came. Others say Jesus mainly means the world will not end until the gospel has done its work in every land.

Jesus points to Daniel's words about "the abomination of desolation." This means something hateful to God that defiles a holy place and brings ruin. Many commentators say it means the Roman army and its idol-like banners standing in and around holy Jerusalem. Others think of an idol set up in the temple. Readers are urged to think hard about what Daniel said.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some commentators think the words "let the reader understand" were added by the Gospel writer to point readers to Daniel, rather than spoken by Jesus.

notes.meaning: When that sign appears, people in Judea should run to the mountains. When God opens a way of escape, it is right to take it. Early church historians say the Christians remembered this warning and fled to Pella, across the Jordan, and were kept safe.

The danger will come so fast that there is no time to grab belongings. Houses had flat roofs with stairs outside, so a person on the roof should leave at once without going in. A worker in the field should not even go back for his coat. Life matters more than things.
Jesus feels deep sorrow for pregnant women and nursing mothers. They will find it hardest to run, and hunger and violence will weigh most heavily on them.

The trouble could not be stopped, but they could pray that it would come at an easier time. Winter would bring cold, mud and short days. On the Sabbath, city gates were shut and many would not travel far. We too may pray that hard things come gently, as God wills.

That time will bring "great tribulation," meaning terrible suffering, worse than any before or after. The historian Josephus describes the siege of Jerusalem with war, famine, disease and fighting inside the city. Some commentators also ask whether these words have a larger meaning still to come.

If God had not limited those days, no one would have survived. But for the sake of "the elect," God's chosen people, He cut them short. The siege ended sooner than expected. Even in judgment, God shows mercy and protects His own.
In desperate times, people grab at any hope of rescue. So when someone says, "Here is the Christ!" do not believe it. The true Christ has already come and is now in heaven.

False christs and false prophets will do amazing signs and wonders. Their tricks will be convincing enough to fool even God's chosen people, if that were possible. Signs and wonders alone do not prove that something is from God. Jesus warns so that His people will stay alert.

differ.view: "If that were possible" means it is not possible. God keeps His chosen ones, and they cannot finally fall away from salvation.

notes.meaning: Jesus has warned them ahead of time. Someone who knows where the attack will come can be ready for it. Because He told us beforehand, we have no excuse to be caught off guard.

If people say the Christ is hiding out in the desert or in some secret room, don't go after them. Many fakes in those days led crowds into the wilderness or to hidden places, and it ended in disaster. Christ is not hidden in a corner, and His people need not chase every new claim.
